name: files
description: File-style storage: root-jailed host/temp filesystems and per-user DLFS drives (decentralised, signed, WebDAV-mountable). Load for reading or writing file content rather than structured lattice values.

content.inline:
## Files
Two mechanisms; pick by need:

**file** — venue-configured roots (host directories, temp scratch, or DLFS-backed drives), root-jailed:
- roots lists what this venue offers; list/tree `{root, path}` browse; read `{root, path}` reads. create `{root, path}` makes an empty file, or add `content: {inline|ref|sha256, contentType?, fileName?}`; it never replaces. path may come from content.fileName. write retains the compact legacy input and explicitly creates-or-overwrites. mkdir creates directories.
- move `{root?, toRoot?, from, to}` renames or relocates; copy uses the same shape. A qualified endpoint `file://<root>/<path>` supplies its own root, so `root` can be omitted; an unqualified `to` defaults to the source root. Conflicting explicit and qualified roots fail.
- Both refuse replacement and dispatch directly through Java NIO. Same-provider operations retain its native fast path; cross-provider efficiency and atomicity depend on those providers. Covia never routes the bytes through model context.
- Also under `v/ops/file/`: append, delete, stat.

**dlfs** — YOUR decentralised drives: per-user, signed, replicated lattice filesystems (also mountable over WebDAV when the venue enables it — mount URL and Windows UNC path at `v/info/adapters/dlfs/webdav`):
- list-drives shows yours; create-drive `{name}` makes one. create works the same way as file:create and uses the same optional content descriptor as assets; read/write transfer file content. Also under `v/ops/dlfs/`: list, tree, mkdir, append, delete, stat, delete-drive.

Choosing storage:
- Structured queryable state -> workspace (`w/`). Immutable shared values -> assets. File-shaped content, external tools, WebDAV access -> dlfs. Host-machine file exchange -> file roots.
- Standard content descriptors use `content.ref` for any resolvable source; `content.dlfs` remains compatible for existing metadata. Add sha256 to pin and verify referenced bytes.
- File ops act on the caller's authority: `file://` roots need explicit capability grants; move needs `crud/write` on both endpoints, while copy needs `crud/read` on the source and `crud/write` on the destination. A copy source may be read-only; move requires both roots writable. Loading this skill grants neither.
